evidence: atptour.com results archive for event 2847/2024 (https://www.atptour.com/en/scores/archive/tenerife/2847/2024/results, accessed 14 Oct 2026): header 'Tenerife 3', '26 Feb - 3 Mar, 2024'; its 31 main-draw results equal the 31 Stage 0 rows match for match (players, winner, every set score and tiebreak, both retirements).
Wikipedia '2024 Tenerife Challenger III' and its singles draw: 26 Feb - 3 Mar 2024, hard; the same 31 results; final Kukushkin d. Gigante 6-2 2-0 ret.

Tenerife 1 (ATP id 9623, 15-21 Jan 2024, Nakashima d. P. Martinez) and Tenerife 2 (ATP id 2839, 19-25 Feb 2024, Gigante d. Travaglia) are different draws on atptour.com and Wikipedia; none of the 31 results is in Tenerife 1 (e.g. there Landaluce lost his R32 to Nakashima and Brancaccio lost his to Barranco Cosano). Stage 0 holds both from Sackmann with their own dates (2024-01-15, 2024-02-19).
atptour.com news of 4 Mar 2024 (kukushkin-gigante-tenerife-challenger-2024-final): the final was played on the Sunday, i.e. 3 Mar 2024.

Mechanism: Tennis My Life's raw 2024_challenger.csv labels all three Tenerife events (ids 2839, 2847, 9623) 'Tenerife 1' with date 20240121, the first event's label copied onto the other two; Stage 0 took 2839 and 9623 from Sackmann but 2847 only from TML (rows 280-310).

Stage 0's convention: of 113 TML-sourced ATP Challenger main-draw events since 2023, 110 are dated on a Monday (their dated matches run from 0 to 6 days after it, medians) and 2 on a Tuesday; 2024-2847 (a Sunday, no dated match) is the only exception. 2024-02-26 is the ATP's start Monday, so the value is unique under the convention (and the timeline's anchor rule maps it to itself); match ids carry no date and stay unchanged.

Now: the 31 rows' windows (19-31 Jan) contain 48 exact-dated matches of the same players elsewhere, e.g. Gigante played the Nonthaburi 3 (Thailand) QF, SF and final on 19-21 Jan, Kukushkin lost the Tenerife 1 QF on 19 Jan and played Ottignies qualifying 22-23 Jan and Koblenz 29-31 Jan, Demin and Landaluce played M15 Manacor 23-26 Jan.

Simulated fix (timing.py's own anchor_day, rule_windows, class windows and draw_narrowing on an in-memory copy; the code reproduces timing.parquet's current windows for all 31): windows R32 23 Feb-3 Mar, R16 25 Feb-4 Mar, QF 27 Feb-5 Mar, SF 27 Feb-6 Mar, F 28 Feb-6 Mar; every match's play day lies inside (31/31; days from the local TennisLive and SofaScore copies, 26 Feb-3 Mar, final 3 Mar as the ATP says); the current windows hold 0/31.
Check (i) after the fix: none of the 32 players has another Stage 0 match dated inside his Tenerife 3 span, nor any other match whose window touches one of his Tenerife 3 play days.

Check (iii) after the fix: in Stage 0's chronological order every player's Tenerife 3 matches are contiguous, follow his previous event (23 of 32 come from Tenerife 2, the rest from Manama, Pune, M15 Villena, M25 Vila Real or AO qualifying) and precede his next (Lugano, Szekesfehervar, Murcia, Miami, ...), days in order.

Size of the present leak (independent code): 136 distinct Stage 0 matches of these players have an earliest start after a misdated result counts (old lf + 1) and before that match was played, as the study says; 171 matches of these players dated 22 Jan - 25 Feb sit after the misdated rows in Stage 0's order although played before them.
No duplicate is created: Stage 0 holds no other copy of Tenerife 3 (its only 2024 Tenerife events are 2839, 2847, 9623).

objections: The two rows are duplicates, not unique records: Stage 0 already holds the same two walkovers from Sackmann, atp|2021-581|Q2|atp:106045|atp:208013 and atp|2021-581|Q2|atp:106408|atp:202103 ('Doha Aus Open Qualies', 2021-01-10; same players, round, winner and W/O). Re-dating keeps each walkover twice, now on the same date and round, so check (i) fails: each of the four players would hold two Q2 rows on the same days.

Check (ii) fails for the fix as proposed (date changed, name 'Australian Open' kept): timing.py then applies the named rule 'Australian Open' 2021 Q2 (schedule_rules.csv, offsets -29..-26 from the main draw's anchor, +-2), anchored on Mon 11 Jan 2021, giving the window 11-18 Dec 2020, which does not hold the Q2 day (12 Jan 2021); each walkover would count from 19 Dec 2020, before it happened. Today's window, 8-15 Jan 2021, holds it, so the timeline does not leak on these rows now. Only re-dating and renaming to the Sackmann event's name gives a window (10-14 Jan) that holds it.
The clear, unique correction is a different operation: drop the two TML rows as duplicates of the Sackmann rows (or merge them into those rows). Setting the date alone is neither unique nor correct.

The date 2021-02-08 follows TML's and the ATP's filing of the 2021 qualifying under the main draw (the ATP's archive lists it under id 580, 8-21 Feb), the usual convention for Slam qualifying. What is corrupt is that these two rows were not merged with Sackmann's own 2021 qualifying event, so they sit four weeks late in Stage 0's order as second copies.
